title: validation_report
description: Machine-readable output of validate-atom-pr. review-pr/fetch.sh consumes this as the evidence base for the (deterministic) validation line. Ported from ROCm/aiter's validate-kernel-pr report_schema.json (commit c1c482e00), trimmed to match validate-atom-pr's deliberately smaller scope: base-vs-head pytest comparison only, no performance scraping, no independent shape grid. Fields that describe coverage stay required precisely so a report cannot overclaim by omission -- where this validator does not perform a stage, the report must say so (status 'skip' plus a reason), never omit the key.

note.description: Required in practice (not just in schema) whenever status is 'skip': the reason a stage was not performed, so the gap reads as a stated scope decision rather than a silent omission.

log.description: Path to the retained stage log.

label.description: Run identifier, e.g. the PR number or a candidate name. Supplied verbatim via --label.

started_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at run start.

isolation.description: The isolation actually achieved, not the isolation intended.

reason.description: Why the level is what it is, when it is not container-level.

arch_coverage.description: Per-architecture coverage. 'runtime' means the selected target was collected and executed with that claimed device visible. An untested architecture is 'not-covered' or absent. validate-atom-pr claims at most one architecture (the GPU it claimed for the run) and never 'compile-only', since it performs no architecture-specific compile step separate from the test run itself.

arch_coverage_basis.description: Per-architecture evidence used to claim runtime coverage, e.g. 'pytest-junit-executed:40'.

degraded_mode.description: NO_GPU means no device was claimed at all. It does not imply that the target needed one -- this validator always attempts a GPU claim and records which device, independent of whether the target under test touches a GPU.

base.description: `git rev-parse HEAD` inside --repo before the candidate patch was applied.

head.description: The --head-sha supplied by the caller, echoed verbatim. validate-atom-pr does not independently re-derive this from content; it is a caller-supplied identity label that fetch.sh's own gate cross-checks against the PR metadata it already holds.

kind.description: Relaxed from aiter's {aiter, flydsl, unknown}: validate-atom-pr only ever validates ROCm/ATOM checkouts.

runtime_identity.description: Interpreter and checkout identity used for the run. Relaxed from aiter's schema: this validator does not resolve a loaded native module's build provenance (no native_artifacts hashing), only the Python/package identity, because it performs no architecture-specific compile step to attest.

native_artifacts.description: Always empty for validate-atom-pr (see description above); the key is kept, not omitted, so a report never silently drops a field fetch.sh's gate still checks the type of.

target.description: Exact pytest node or file selected by the caller via --target.

shape_env.description: Always empty: validate-atom-pr injects no independent shape grid.

grid.description: Always empty: no shape grid is supplied or consumed. See the correctness_s1_grid stage for the explicit skip reason.

expected_route.description: Relaxed from aiter: validate-atom-pr performs no route/kernel-symbol instrumentation (see the execution_receipt stage), so this is never a real dispatch route -- it is always the fixed string 'not-derived: route detection is out of scope for validate-atom-pr', kept non-empty only so fetch.sh's existing required-field check (ported from a richer validator) still sees a stated value rather than a silently missing one.

shape_vars.description: Relaxed the same way as expected_route, for the same reason: always 'not-derived: shape-grid instrumentation is out of scope for validate-atom-pr'.

stages.description: One entry per stage. A stage that was not performed reports 'skip' with a note; it never reports 'pass' or 'info' for work it did not do. correctness_s1_grid, execution_receipt and index_width_scan are permanently 'skip' for validate-atom-pr -- they name real work (shape-grid execution, runtime route instrumentation, and the static index-width scan fetch.sh already runs separately) that this minimal validator deliberately does not perform, by the user's own scope decision, not by omission.

merge_sim.description: Candidate patch applied onto the recorded base; conflict short-circuits the run.

gpu_claim.description: GPU claimed and recorded, independent of whether --target needs one.

idleness_basis.description: Relaxed from aiter's {activity+vram, vram-only, unknown}: on this box, rocm-smi's product-name lookup fails outright ('Error when calling libdrm'), so validate-atom-pr does not attempt the richer vram-based classification aiter's pick-idle-gpu.py does -- it either measures gfx busy-% via `rocm-smi --showuse` ('activity') or, if that call itself fails, honestly records 'unknown' rather than inventing a basis.

runtime_compat.description: Whether `import atom` resolves inside the supplied --repo checkout rather than some other installed copy.

test_policy.description: The --target collects at least one test item before either run starts, so a target that cannot even be collected is reported as such rather than silently producing a hollow 'pass'.

baseline_control.description: --target run at base (before the patch is applied). Without this, 'head fails' and 'was already failing' are indistinguishable.

correctness_repo_tests.description: --target run at head (the patch applied on top of base).

correctness_s1_grid.description: Independent shape-grid execution. Out of scope for validate-atom-pr by decision -- always 'skip'.

execution_receipt.description: Proof that a named kernel route was actually reached at runtime. Out of scope for validate-atom-pr by decision -- always 'skip'.

index_width_scan.description: Static index x stride overflow scan. Performed separately by review-pr/fetch.sh via scan_index_width.py and not duplicated here -- always 'skip'.

verdict.description: PASS: base and head both pass (head may fix a pre-existing base failure -- noted in findings). BLOCK: base passes, head fails -- this PR introduced it. NEEDS_WORK: base and head both fail -- pre-existing, not this PR's fault. INCONCLUSIVE: an earlier stage (merge_sim/gpu_claim/runtime_compat/test_policy) could not be completed, so base and head were never both actually run.
